source_interpretation.title: Crystallite, particle and accessible surface are different quantities
source_interpretation.text: The authors associate low BET area in low-water mixtures with sulfate-associated aggregation. Run3 has2.7nm Scherrer crystallites but about10nm TEM particles/aggregates; the reported particle-to-crystallite size ratio is3.7. This does not make the crystallites individually10nm. Runs4–7 surface-area estimates are described as comparable to crystallite size, suggesting single crystals; that is an interpretation, not atomic structural evidence.
source_interpretation.source_locator: Supplied main pp.2–3, BET and TEM discussion

source_interpretation.title: Water, alcohol and reflux time affect the reported outcomes
source_interpretation.text: The authors propose that water and higher reflux temperatures favor hydrolysis, while adsorbed alcohol obstructs it. The table retains all individual outcomes, including the nonmonotonic low-water sizes. No unreported mixture boiling temperatures or continuous size predictor are supplied.
source_interpretation.source_locator: Supplied main p.2, hydrolysis and solvent discussion

source_interpretation.title: Surface cleaning depends on the treatment
source_interpretation.text: Ammonia washing is associated with sulfate removal and higher surface area. Heating the ammonia-washed product at400°C for1h removes adsorbed ammonia; heating at600°C is associated with sulfate combustion and larger crystallites. The source does not establish that600°C material followed the ammonia/400°C sequence.

missingness: All three supplied main pages, Table I, Figures 1–3 and fourteen bibliographic entries were read; SI and cited full texts remain unreviewed.
Reflux temperatures are not reported individually. The conclusion states synthesis below 100 °C; this is a strict study-wide upper bound, not a measured temperature assigned to each solvent mixture.

Vessel geometry/capacity, stirring rate, heating ramp, atmosphere during reflux/annealing, centrifugation duration/RCF, washing volumes/repetitions, vacuum pressure, numeric drying temperature and product storage are unreported. Overnight drying is not converted to hours.
Scherrer crystallite sizes, approximate TEM aggregate diameter and BET surface area are separate quantities. No measured atomic coordinates, size distribution or raw curves are available.
Yield is source-calculated from precipitate mass with chemisorbed sulfate evaluated by TG-DTA; rows 11/12 contain dashes, not zero yields.
Run 12 Table I footnote states 600 °C for 1 h without ammonia washing; no ammonia step or 400 °C predecessor is inherited. Its exact physical parent specimen is unreported.
Runs 10–12 are supporting post-treatment comparisons using the row-3 preparation framework; they are not new independent growth routes or asserted physical replicates.
Source reports 6.6 wt% sulfate for H2O/EtOH = 250/0, outside the twelve tabulated runs; it is retained as unassigned contextual evidence rather than invented as run 5 or a complete new recipe.
Full molecular/crystal presentation remains pending. Generic molecule references and stage diagrams are explanatory, not measured solution or apparatus geometry.
